tasks.short: Collect the job order and drawing, read blueprints for specifications and tooling, look up settings from earlier runs, plan the sequence of operations across machines, and note changes for next time.

steps.what: Machine setter collects the paper job order and drawing from the planner
Machine setter reads blueprints and job orders to determine product specifications and tooling instructions
Machine setter looks up tools and settings from earlier runs in a notebook
Machine setter plans operational sequences across the machines
Machine setter notes setting changes for the next run: in a notebook today, on the part's setup sheet after the change

tasks.design: Job orders arrive on the shop-floor terminal from the MES ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with the current drawing revision attached. A setup sheet per part number holds the tool list, settings and notes from earlier runs, so the setter does not search a notebook, and changes are saved on the sheet. Reading drawings and planning the sequence stay with the setter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job orders and drawings were paper, and settings lived in personal notebooks.
tasks.enabler_now: MES terminals show job orders, drawings and setup sheets per part.
tasks.still_hard: Notes from experienced setters are hard to get onto the sheet.
tasks.human_edge: Planning the order of jobs so the slow machine never waits.

evidence.claim: MES terminals can show job orders with drawings and setup sheets per part number.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the planned job to updated setup notes; setting up the machines is outside.
Input contract: drawings from engineering via the MES; fallback is paper job orders and notebooks.
Reading, planning and noting changes keep their full time; the note is a first record. s1 keeps 30 for jobs that still come on paper; s3 keeps 40 for reading the sheet and for parts without one.
Setters share their notes on the setup sheet.

incremental.description: Machine setter fixes wrong or outdated entries on setup sheets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many new parts without earlier runs and some jobs still on paper, so half of the lookups and collections stay (13.0); high: mostly repeat parts with setup sheets (22.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pick tools and holding devices from the crib, measure tool lengths and offsets, check them, enter offsets in the machine control, and install and align drills, cutters, dies, guides and fixtures.

steps.what: Machine setter selects drills, cutters and holding devices from the tool crib
Machine setter measures tool lengths and diameters: by hand at the spindle today, by mounting each tool on the presetter after the change
Machine setter checks the measured tool offsets: each value against the tool and the tool number the program calls
Machine setter loads the checked offsets into the machine control: typed in today, sent from the presetter in one load after the change
Machine setter installs and adjusts alignment of drills, cutters, dies, guides and holding devices using templates, measuring instruments and hand tools

tasks.design: The setup sheet in the MES ({OPS_SYSTEM}) lists each tool with its crib location, so tools are picked without searching. Tools are measured on a presetter outside the machine instead of by hand at the spindle; the setter checks the values and loads the checked offsets once into the machine control over the network. Installing and aligning tools, dies and fixtures stay with the setter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tools were found by searching the crib and measured by hand on the machine, with offsets typed in.
tasks.enabler_now: Tool presetters measure outside the machine and send offsets to CNC controls.
tasks.still_hard: Older machines without a network link still need offsets typed in.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that a die sits slightly off and shimming it.

reach.learn: Whether presetting moves to the crib.

evidence.claim: Tool presetters measure tool length and diameter outside the machine and can send offsets to CNC controls.

assumptions: Boundary: from the tool list to the machine set up; the first-off check is outside.
Input contract: tool lists from the setup sheet; crib locations kept by the crib attendant; fallback is searching and hand measurement.

Installing, aligning and the offset check keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because walking to the crib stays and only the search goes; s2 keeps 50 because each tool is still mounted on the presetter; s4 keeps 10 for the load itself.
Presetter values are checked before each load.
unknowns: CNC machines with a network link.
research_questions: Do offset errors on first parts fall?

incremental.description: Machine setter keeps crib locations current on setup sheets.

approvals.approved_version: The tool offsets per tool number exactly as checked by the setter in s3, loaded once into the control of the machine being set up; any change needs a new check and load.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most machines are older ones without a network link, so offsets are still typed in and many tools measured at the spindle (9.0); high: CNC machines linked to the presetter (24.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch the running machines for malfunctions, measure sample parts for defects, adjust machines as needed, and write measurements on the control chart.

steps.what: Machine setter observes machine operation to detect malfunctions
Machine setter measures sample parts to detect workpiece defects
Machine setter writes measurements on the paper control chart
Machine setter adjusts machines as necessary

tasks.design: Machine monitoring ({OPS_SYSTEM}) reads each machine's status from its control and shows stops and alarms on a screen and a light, so the setter goes to the machine that needs attention instead of walking every machine. Gauges with a data output send measurements to the control chart in the same system, which flags drift. Measuring parts and adjusting machines stay with the setter; status data are kept per machine, not used to rate operators.
tasks.previous_blocker: The setter walked between machines to see their state and wrote measurements by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine monitoring reads machine states from controls; gauges send readings to control charts.
tasks.still_hard: Many defects show only when a part is measured.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a tool start to chatter before the part goes out of tolerance.

reach.learn: Whether digital charts show drift earlier.

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X Machine Monitoring collects produced quantities and machine statuses from the machine control and assigns them to the workplace.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from running machines to the machine adjusted; maintenance repairs are outside.
Input contract: machine states from controls; measurements from gauges with data output; fallback is walking and paper charts.
Measuring and adjusting do not change.
Older machines get a simple signal from their stack light.
research_questions: Do machines stand still for shorter times?

incremental.description: Machine setter clears false alarms from the monitoring screen.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few machines per setter and half of the gauges without data output, so walking and writing stay for many checks (7.7); high: monitoring and data gauges as designed (16.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the job's coolant and lubricant needs, test coolant concentration, select coolants and lubricants and top up, start their flow, and log readings.

steps.what: Machine setter checks the job's coolant and lubricant needs in the job papers
Machine setter tests coolant concentration with a refractometer
Machine setter selects the proper coolants and lubricants and tops up
Machine setter starts the coolant flow and checks the nozzles
Machine setter writes concentration readings in the paper coolant log

tasks.design: The setup sheet in the MES ({OPS_SYSTEM}) states the coolant type and target concentration per material, so the setter does not look them up in job papers. Readings are entered on the terminal, which shows the trend per machine and flags readings outside the target. Testing, selecting, topping up and starting the flow stay with the setter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coolant needs were found in job papers and readings written in a paper log.
tasks.enabler_now: MES setup sheets and terminals can hold coolant targets and readings.
tasks.still_hard: Coolant condition shows in smell and colour as much as in readings.
tasks.human_edge: Smelling that a coolant tank has gone bad.

reach.learn: Whether trends show when a tank needs cleaning.

evidence.claim: MES setup sheets and terminals can hold coolant targets per material and log readings per machine.

assumptions: Boundary: from the job order to the coolant flowing; tank cleaning is outside.
Input contract: coolant targets set by the process engineer; fallback is job papers and the paper log.
Testing, topping up and starting the flow do not change.
s5 is the first record of the concentration readings and keeps its full time; transcribing readings into the production record is cut in sibling task 10219.
research_questions: Are tanks cleaned before coolant goes bad?

incremental.description: Machine setter reports wrong coolant targets on setup sheets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one coolant for most jobs, so the setter rarely looked needs up and the sheet saves little (3.5); high: several coolants for different materials (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The machine setter keeps reading drawings, setting up, aligning, measuring and adjusting; paper job orders, notebooks, hand-measured offsets and paper charts shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using setup sheets and machine monitoring
role.ambitious_version: A setter who runs more machines with fewer surprises.

job.title: Multiple Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
